evals.name: eval-set-size-and-effect-size
evals.prompt: We have an internal support agent and 12 test tasks. My lead says 12 is too few to tell whether a prompt change helped. How big an improvement should we expect from prompt changes this early, and is 12 enough? Back it up with whatever evidence exists.
assertions: If the answer mentions the 30% to 80% figure, it presents it as a hypothetical or illustration, not as something Anthropic measured or observed (pass if the figure is absent)
Recommends repeating each task several times (multiple trials) or otherwise accounting for run-to-run variance
Mentions the 20-50 tasks drawn from real failures starting point
Does not invent a statistic that is absent from the skill's sources

evals.name: code-actions-vs-json
evals.prompt: I'm using smolagents. Should my agent write Python code actions instead of JSON tool calls? I heard code actions take fewer steps. I'd just run them with the default local executor on my laptop.
assertions: If a step-reduction or success figure for code actions is cited, it is attributed to research (CodeAct / Wang et al.) or to the smolagents README citing research, not described as Hugging Face's own benchmark (pass if no figure is cited)
States that smolagents' local Python executor is not a security sandbox
Names the operational cost of code execution (sandboxing, resource limits, or monitoring)
Gives a verdict in the first two sentences

evals.name: reliability-research
evals.prompt: Our agent hits 85% on our eval and leadership wants to call it production-ready. What does recent research say reliability means beyond a pass rate? Be specific about the studies.
assertions: If the Rabanser et al. / Princeton reliability study's model count is given, it is 15 (fail if it says 14)
Names at least three of: consistency, robustness, predictability, safety
Explains pass^k (all k trials succeed) versus pass@k
Does not invent figures or studies that are absent from the skill's sources

evals.name: mcp-server-sampling-and-confirmation
evals.prompt: I'm designing an MCP server against the 2026-07-28 spec. One tool needs to call an LLM to summarize long documents, and another sometimes has to ask the user to confirm a choice in the middle of the call. It also needs to remember which document set the user picked across calls. What's the right design?
assertions: Advises against MCP Sampling for the LLM call (deprecated) and recommends calling the LLM provider directly
For mid-call user confirmation, recommends returning an input_required result / multi round-trip request with a client retry, rather than a server-initiated elicitation/create request
Keeps cross-call state in server-minted handles passed as tool arguments, not protocol sessions
Does not recommend Mcp-Session-Id or protocol-level sessions

evals.name: email-agent-prompt-injection
evals.targets: audit item 4 (Rule of Two originals); regression control
evals.prompt: My email-triage agent reads inbound customer emails, can look up accounts in our CRM, and can send replies on its own. Someone on the team asked whether it's safe against prompt injection. What should I tell them and what should I change?
assertions: Identifies that the agent holds all three properties (untrusted input, private data, external communication / state change)
Recommends a human approval on the combining step or splitting the work so no session holds all three
Names at least one non-obvious exfiltration channel (image URL, link, API parameter)
Leads with a verdict (not safe as designed, or equivalent) in the first two sentences

evals.name: parallel-coding-agents
evals.prompt: I want to run 4 coding agents in parallel on the same repo, each owning one feature, so we ship faster. Good idea? If not, what multi-agent setup does work for coding?
assertions: Warns that parallel agents writing to shared code make conflicting decisions
Proposes a setup where subagents read/explore and one agent owns writes, or a separate reviewer agent with a clean context
Does not present Cognition as opposing all multi-agent setups without qualification (pass if Cognition is not mentioned)
Leads with a verdict in the first two sentences

evals.name: long-coding-task-structure
evals.prompt: Our coding agent keeps running out of context on big refactors in a 400k-line monorepo. How should we structure these tasks?
assertions: Recommends a research then plan then implement structure, or equivalent phased approach with subagents for exploration
Does not state a specific plan length in lines (e.g. 'a couple hundred lines') as sourced guidance
If the 40-60% context utilization target is mentioned, it is attributed to practitioners/HumanLayer rather than to Anthropic
Recommends a durable notes/progress file or compaction

evals.name: fabricated-order-status
evals.prompt: Our support agent sometimes tells customers an order 'shipped yesterday' when the order lookup tool actually returned nothing. We've added 'never make up order status' to the prompt three times. What's going on?
assertions: Says more prompting is not the fix (verdict that this is a harness/verification problem)
Recommends a sanctioned failure outcome (an explicit 'could not find' result the harness accepts)
Recommends checking the actual tool-call record or response rather than the model's claim
Proposes a concrete test or diagnostic (e.g. sort transcripts into causes) before committing to a fix

evals.name: mcp-tool-output-cap
evals.prompt: My MCP tool returns full log files and Claude Code keeps cutting them off. What's the actual limit, and how should I redesign the tool?
assertions: States Claude Code's default MCP tool output cap is 25,000 tokens
Mentions a way to change the limit (MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS or a per-tool limit)
Recommends redesigning the tool to filter/search/paginate rather than return full logs
Makes truncation visible and recoverable (e.g. offset/next-page hint)

evals.name: memory-stale-preference
evals.prompt: Our assistant stores user preferences in a vector DB and retrieves the top 10 on every turn. Users complain it keeps using their old address after they told it they moved. We added 'always prefer the most recent information' to the prompt. Fix?
assertions: Says the prompt rule is not the fix (verdict in first two sentences)
Recommends explicit invalidation/supersession of the old fact on write rather than resolving conflicts at read time
Recommends narrower retrieval or a structured (key-value) store for preferences instead of top-10 on every turn
If research is cited, attributes it correctly (e.g. MemoryAgentBench, TEPA) and does not invent figures
Proposes a test with an update/reversal across sessions

evals.name: memory-for-coding-agent
evals.targets: memory.md: whether memory is worth it
evals.prompt: Should I add Mem0 or another long-term memory product to my coding agent that works on one repo?
assertions: Verdict that it is probably unnecessary, given in the first two sentences
Explains that repo files and a progress/notes file already hold the state
Recommends testing against a no-memory baseline before adopting
Does not claim a memory product is generally superior to plain retrieval

evals.name: compaction-choice
evals.prompt: Our SWE agent's context fills up. Should we build an LLM summarizer for old turns, or is there something simpler?
assertions: Recommends trying observation masking / clearing old tool results first
If The Complexity Trap or similar research is cited, states masking matched summarization at about half the cost of the raw agent, without inflating the result
Mentions that summaries can lose identifiers or details and recommends keeping decisions/identifiers verbatim (notes file)
Mentions checking prompt-cache impact or cost before and after

evals.name: multi-agent-equal-budget
evals.prompt: Our 4-agent debate setup beat our single agent by 6 points on our QA eval. Proof that multi-agent is better, right?
assertions: Asks whether both systems had the same token/compute budget, or states the comparison is confounded without it
Cites equal-budget evidence (e.g. Tran and Kiela 2026) accurately if cited, scoped to multi-hop QA
Recommends repeated trials and a paired comparison rather than one run
Leads with a verdict (not proven yet) in the first two sentences

evals.name: mcp-tool-poisoning
evals.prompt: We let users connect any MCP server from a public list to our agent, which also has access to their Google Drive. Anything to worry about?
assertions: Identifies tool poisoning / instructions in tool descriptions or results as a risk
Notes that annotations from untrusted servers must not be trusted
Recommends pinning versions or diffing tool definitions on update
Applies the Rule of Two (untrusted server text + Drive data + an outbound channel) and recommends gating or isolation
States that being listed in a registry is not a security review (pass if the registry is not mentioned)

evals.name: injection-defense-claim
evals.prompt: A vendor says their prompt-injection classifier blocks 99.5% of attacks on a benchmark. Can we rely on it and drop the human approval step on outbound emails?
assertions: Says no, keep the structural control, in the first two sentences
Explains that defenses tested on static attacks fail under adaptive attacks, citing The Attacker Moves Second accurately if cited
Recommends structural controls (approval, plan-then-execute, quarantine/dual LLM, egress allowlist) with the classifier as one layer
Does not invent attack-success figures

evals.name: framework-choice-hitl
evals.prompt: Which framework should I use for an agent that must pause up to a day for a manager to approve refunds, then continue? We're on Python and use several model providers.
assertions: Names serializable pause/resume state as the deciding requirement
Mentions at least two concrete mechanisms by their documented names (e.g. LangGraph interrupt + checkpointer, OpenAI Agents SDK RunState, Pydantic AI deferred tools, ADK confirmations)
Flags idempotency of side effects on resume
Notes that versions/defaults change and should be checked, or gives an as-of date

evals.name: inspect-eval-setup
evals.prompt: How do I measure pass^k for my tool-using agent with Inspect AI? Give me the key pieces.
assertions: Uses Epochs with the pass_k(k) reducer (or 'pass_k_{k}') for pass^k, and distinguishes it from pass_at(k)
States k must not exceed the number of epochs
Recommends an outcome-based custom scorer rather than only checking the final text
Mentions sandboxing or message/token limits

evals.name: harness-regression-tests
evals.prompt: We changed our agent harness's retry logic and now worry that a crash mid-run could charge customers twice. How should we test this?
assertions: Recommends deterministic tests with a scripted/mock model rather than only running evals
Describes a crash-then-resume test asserting the side-effecting tool ran once
Recommends idempotency keys for the charge operation
Asserts on the tool-call/event log rather than model text

evals.name: benchmark-validity
evals.prompt: We built 60 eval tasks for our booking agent and it scores 92%. Anything we should check before believing that?
assertions: Recommends running a do-nothing or trivial agent against the suite
Recommends checking graders verify the actual outcome rather than the agent's claim, and closing shortcuts
Recommends reading transcripts
If ABC/BenchJack/HAL are cited, the figures match the sources (e.g. 38% do-nothing on tau-bench airline)

evals.name: cache-cost-jump
evals.prompt: After we added the current time and the user's name to the top of our agent's system prompt, our token bill nearly doubled even though conversations didn't get longer. Why?
assertions: Explains that changing early content breaks prompt-cache prefix reuse on every call
Recommends moving per-call variables to the end or out of the prefix
Mentions other cache breakers (tool order changes, editing earlier messages) or measuring cache hit rate
Does not attribute the cause to context length

note: A/B regression prompts. 1-9 from the 2026-10-18 audit; 10-20 added 2026-11-02 for memory, compaction, multi-agent budgets, MCP, injection, frameworks, Inspect AI, harness testing, benchmark validity, and caching. Each assertion is checked against verified source facts; run old and new skill versions 3x per prompt and compare.
